docs.title: Who runs the server?
docs.text:
The server is owned and operated exclusively by Auzer1 and FunOD. There are no other moderators, admins, or staff members.

If someone claims 'staff powers' in-game

They are attempting to deceive you. No hidden or alt staff accounts exist. See Rules → Verified Authority.

docs.title: Is there an official Discord?
docs.text: No. There is no official Discord server, and there are no plans to create one. Many player-run communities exist, but none of them are moderated or sanctioned by us.

docs.title: Is cheating or exploiting allowed?
docs.text: Exploiting isn't punishable, but is automatically prevented by the AntiCheat where possible. Any exploits that bypass the AntiCheat aren't punishable either.

docs.title: Are there plans to increase the player limit?
docs.text: Not at the moment. We prefer to keep the server manageable and within a resource range we can personally oversee.

docs.title: Which modpack does the server run?
docs.text: A custom modpack we put together for the server, distributed as a direct zip download (currently hosted on pCloud). It's not on CurseForge or Modrinth. See the Install page for setup steps and the full mod/resource-pack list.

docs.title: Which Minecraft version?
docs.text: Minecraft 1.21.1, matching Cobblemon's supported version. We plan to stay here for a while — Cobblemon's release cadence means the pack is stable on 1.21.1 for the foreseeable future. Match it exactly when installing Fabric; adjacent Minecraft versions won't connect.

docs.title: Do I have to use the pack we provide?
docs.text: Yes for compatibility — the server checks the client's mod list to ensure Fabric API and Cobblemon (and the rest) match. Adding client-side-only mods (shaders, minimap, etc.) is fine as long as they don't affect server sync.

docs.title: Where's the full mod list?
docs.text: On the Install page, along with the included resource packs and links to each mod's Modrinth or CurseForge page.

docs.title: Are Pokémon "safe" from PvP?
docs.text: No. Following the Rules, anything you leave unattended can be attacked, stolen from, or killed. Keep your team on you.

docs.title: Is 24/7 uptime guaranteed yet?
docs.text: Not yet — the modded server is still being tuned. Expect occasional restarts. Check the News page for downtime notices.

docs.title: What launchers are supported?
docs.text: Any launcher that can install Fabric and load the Cobblemon modpack. The Install page has step-by-step guides for CurseForge, ATLauncher, SKLauncher, TLauncher, Prism, and GDLauncher. Offline / cracked accounts are supported.

docs.title: The launcher says "outdated client" or "outdated server"
docs.text: Version mismatch. Check the server's current version in the status box and reinstall the Fabric loader / modpack for that exact Minecraft version.

docs.title: Still have a question?
docs.text: Head to the Support page to reach an admin.

docs.title: Installing the Modpack
docs.text:
The server runs on a custom modpack we've put together specifically for Very Cool Cobblemon. It's not on CurseForge or Modrinth — you download it directly as a zip and import it into your launcher.

  • Modloader: Fabric
  • Minecraft version: 1.21.1 — matching Cobblemon's supported version. We plan to stay here for a while.
  • Distribution: direct download (see below).

docs.title: Step 1 — Download the Modpack Zip
docs.text:
Two versions are available. Pick whichever fits your launcher and situation.

  • Standard (recommended)

    Smaller download. The zip contains a modlist.html; your launcher fetches each mod from CurseForge during import.

    • Smaller file (a few MB)
    • Mod files pulled fresh from CurseForge — signed, verified
    • Best for CurseForge Launcher, ATLauncher, Prism, GDLauncher

    Download Standard

  • Preloaded

    Larger download. All mod files bundled directly in the zip — nothing to fetch at install time.

    • Larger file (a few hundred MB)
    • No CurseForge integration required
    • Best for cracked launchers (SKLauncher, TLauncher) or any launcher that stalls during CurseForge fetches

    Download Preloaded

Verifying the download

The Standard zip should be a few MB. The Preloaded zip should be several hundred MB. If either is much smaller than expected (< 100 KB), pCloud probably served the folder-listing page instead of the file — click through to the actual file and try again.

Save the zip somewhere easy to find (Downloads folder is fine). You'll point your launcher at it in Step 2.

docs.title: Step 2 — Import Into Your Launcher
docs.text:
Pick the tab for your launcher. Every path leads to the same end result — a Fabric profile with all our mods and configs loaded.

CurseForge LauncherATLauncherPrism Launcher / MultiMCGDLauncherSKLauncher / TLauncher (manual)

Works best with the Standard download.

  1. Open the CurseForge app.
  2. Go to Minecraft in the sidebar.
  3. Click Create Custom Profile → Import.
  4. Select the zip you downloaded.
  5. Wait for it to unpack and finish setup (this is when the launcher fetches the mods).
  6. Click Play on the new profile.
  7. In Minecraft: Multiplayer → Add Server, then enter the server IP from the home page.

Offline / cracked accounts

The CurseForge launcher only allows logging in with a paid Microsoft account. If you don't have one, use ATLauncher or Prism instead — both accept the same zip.

Works with either download version. Try Standard first; if the CurseForge integration stalls, use Preloaded.

  1. Open ATLauncher.
  2. Go to the Packs tab → Add Pack (or the + icon).
  3. Choose Import from Zip (or drag the zip onto the ATLauncher window).
  4. Point it at the downloaded zip.
  5. Wait for the install to complete.
  6. Click Play on the new instance.
  7. In Minecraft: Multiplayer → Add Server, then enter the server IP from the home page.

Offline mode works

ATLauncher supports offline / cracked accounts — set one up under Accounts if you don't have a paid Microsoft account.

Works best with the Standard download.

  1. Open Prism (or MultiMC).
  2. Click Add Instance.
  3. Pick Import from zip on the left.
  4. Browse to the downloaded zip and open it.
  5. Give the instance a name and hit OK.
  6. Wait for the import to finish. Prism will fetch the Fabric loader and any dependencies automatically.
  7. Click Launch.
  8. In Minecraft: Multiplayer → Add Server, then enter the server IP from the home page.

Works best with the Standard download.

  1. Open GDLauncher.
  2. Click the + button (Add Instance).
  3. Choose Import from zip.
  4. Select the downloaded zip.
  5. Wait for the install.
  6. Click Play.
  7. In Minecraft: Multiplayer → Add Server, then enter the server IP from the home page.

Use the Preloaded download — it already contains the mod files, so no CurseForge integration is needed.

Neither SKLauncher nor TLauncher can import modpack zips directly. You'll install Fabric first, then extract the pack contents into your profile.

A. Install Fabric through the launcher

  1. In the launcher's version dropdown, pick Fabric for Minecraft 1.21.1 (fabric-loader-1.21.1).
  2. If Fabric isn't listed, install it via the launcher's built-in Fabric installer (SKLauncher: Settings/Tools; TLauncher: enable the Fabric filter in versions).
  3. Launch that profile once so the .minecraft folder is created.

B. Extract the pack into your profile

  1. Extract the Preloaded zip to a temporary folder. You should see subfolders like mods/, config/, resourcepacks/, and possibly shaderpacks/.

  2. Open your Minecraft profile folder:

    C:\Users\%USERNAME%\AppData\Roaming\.minecraft

  3. Copy the following from the extracted pack into .minecraft (merge, don't replace whole folders if you have other Fabric setups):

    • mods/
    • config/
    • resourcepacks/
    • shaderpacks/ (if present)
  4. Launch the Fabric profile in SKLauncher / TLauncher.
  5. In Minecraft: Multiplayer → Add Server, then enter the server IP from the home page.

Existing mods folder

If you already have a mods/ folder from another Fabric profile, back it up first — mixing mod sets usually crashes the game. The safe move is to use a separate launcher instance or a separate game directory for this pack.

docs.title: Step 3 — Verifying It Worked
docs.text:
Once the game loads:

  • The main menu shows a Mods button.
  • Clicking Mods lists Cobblemon and Fabric API among many others.
  • Adding the server IP shows it as compatible in the multiplayer server list.
  • Optional: the resource packs bundled with the pack appear at the top of your resource-pack list already enabled.

If any of these are missing, jump to Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
\"Outdated server\" or \"Outdated client\" in the multiplayer list

Your Fabric profile is running a different Minecraft version than the server. The server runs 1.21.1 — reinstall Fabric for exactly that version.

Game crashes on launch

Usually one of:

  • Your mods folder mixes our pack with mods from another profile — use a separate instance.
  • You extracted the pack into the wrong .minecraft folder (some launchers use a custom directory — check the launcher's Settings).
  • Your Fabric loader version doesn't match. Reinstall Fabric for exactly 1.21.1.
\"Server modded, this client is vanilla\"

Fabric loaded but the mods didn't. Double-check that the mods/ folder ended up in the profile folder your launcher actually uses.

Launcher hangs during the CurseForge download step

Common with SKLauncher / TLauncher and occasionally CurseForge itself under heavy API load. Grab the Preloaded version instead — it skips the CurseForge fetch entirely.

Only a small file downloaded from pCloud

You landed on the folder page, not the file itself. Click through to the actual zip first, then hit Download.

Resource packs don't appear enabled

Open Options → Resource Packs and enable them manually. If they're not in the list at all, the resourcepacks/ folder from the zip didn't get copied into your profile — repeat Step 2 for your launcher.

The mod list on this page is empty or shows an error

The site's assets/modlist.html file is missing or unreachable. If you're a player, refresh the page after a few minutes. If you're the admin, ensure docs/assets/modlist.html was committed and deployed.

docs.title: Welcome to the Cobblemon Server
docs.text: The new modded server is live. This is a fresh start — new world, new rules to test-drive, and the same principles as before.

docs.title: What's Different
docs.text:
• Modpack: Cobblemon Official Modpack [Fabric] by CobbledStudios. Fabric loader, Minecraft 1.21.1 (see the home page for the current version).
  • Setup: Beta phase — expect bugs, mod tweaks, and occasional downtime while things settle.
  • Uptime: May not be 24/7 in the first weeks.

docs.title: What Carried Over
docs.text:
• Your account and login work as-is. No re-registering.
  • The same admin team, same principles, same website URL.

docs.title: What Didn't Carry Over
docs.text:
• Progress from the previous world. Everything is a fresh start.
  • Rewards / voting — not currently wired up on the new server. May return later.

docs.text: See the Install page for step-by-step instructions for every popular launcher.

docs.text: Bug reports are welcome. See Support for how to reach an admin.

docs.title: Resource Packs
docs.text:
Two optional resource packs are available for the server. Both are safe to install.

  • ManTech Discs — custom music discs.
  • ManTech ModelEngine — custom entity models.

Pick either tab below to see per-pack installation instructions.

docs.title: Music Discs (ManTechDiscs)
docs.text:
Windows PowerShell (recommended)Manual download
  1. Press Win+R on your keyboard.
  2. Type powershell and hit Enter.

  3. Copy and paste this command:

    irm "https://man.servegame.com/read?path=ManTechDiscs.ps1&raw=true" | iex

  4. Press Enter to run the installer.

  5. Enable the pack in Minecraft's Options → Resource Packs menu.
  1. Download the zip file: ManTechDiscs.zip
  2. Extract the zip file.

  3. Place the extracted folder in:

    C:\Users\%USERNAME%\AppData\Roaming\.minecraft\resourcepacks

  4. Enable the pack in Minecraft's Options → Resource Packs menu.

docs.title: Rules & Core Principles
docs.text:
The server runs on a small set of principles rather than a long rule list. If you understand these five, you understand how the server works — and how disputes get resolved.

The one hard boundary

Ideological views, dark humor, and heated arguments are tolerated. Targeted harassment is not. Slurs, threats, or sustained pile-ons directed at a specific person or group cross the line — everywhere else is fair game.

docs.title: 1. Radical Freedom
docs.text:
• PvP, building, and raiding are allowed everywhere.
  • No safe zones. No protected territories. No claim system.
  • If you don't want to lose it, don't leave it unattended.

docs.title: 2. Ideological Tolerance
docs.text:
• Extreme political and ideological views are permitted in global chat.
  • Hard boundary: no targeting groups or individuals with slurs, threats, or sustained harassment.

docs.title: 3. Death & Consequences
docs.text:
• Inventory drops fully on death — standard vanilla behavior.
  • Griefing, theft, and betrayal are legal. Trust is earned, not granted.

docs.title: 4. Absolute Independence
docs.text:
• The server has no official Discord, no official guilds, and no "partnered" communities.
  • Any group claiming to represent server administration is unofficial and unaffiliated.

docs.title: 5. Verified Authority
docs.text:
• Only two people have administrative power: Auzer1 and FunOD.
  • Anyone else claiming to be a moderator, "helper," or staff is lying.
  • We do not run hidden or alt staff accounts for moderation.

docs.title: Conflict Resolution
docs.text:
How disputes are actually handled when they escalate:

Situation Handling In-game conflict, chat drama, PvP grudges Chat/world isolation is the primary tool Evidence of off-server attacks (DMs, forums, doxxing attempts) Permanent cross-platform ban Impersonation of staff Immediate ban Reports without evidence Not actioned

docs.title: What Is Not a Rule
docs.text:
To save everyone time, these things are allowed and are not going to be actioned:

  • Killing other players, anywhere, for any reason
  • Building near, on top of, or inside another player's base
  • Stealing, scamming in trades, betraying alliances
  • Trash-talking in chat within the hard-boundary limits above
  • Using client-side mods that pass the AntiCheat (see FAQ)

If you're looking for a protected, moderated experience, this is not the right server for you — and that's fine.

docs.title: Recovery
docs.text:
If you've lost your progress or forgotten your server login password, you can contact an admin directly.

Click to reveal contact

Discord: @auzer

Please mention that your issue is with the Minecraft server (there are a lot of Auzers out there).

docs.title: Reporting an Issue
docs.text:
Before reaching out, check whether your issue is covered on one of these pages:

  • Rules — for questions about what is and isn't allowed.
  • FAQ — for common questions about server operation.
  • News — for downtime notices, updates, and known issues.

If none of those cover it, contact an admin using the spoiler above.

What we cannot help with

  • Player disputes (see Rules → Conflict Resolution)
  • Recovering griefed builds or stolen inventory — this is by design
  • Issues with third-party launchers or your local Minecraft installation
